title: Prompt engineering in LLMs for automated unit test generation: A large-scale study
read_source: Author-posted manuscript via ORBilu institutional repository: https://orbilu.uni.lu/bitstream/10993/68099/1/s10664-026-10840-4.pdf (58 pages, 22,895 extracted words; published EMSE 31(4), Article 103, 28 March 2026). The local Springer HTML file is only a paywall/abstract page and is not counted as the read source.
datasets: Defects4J: token-filtered class-level dataset, 477 classes across 16 projects; underlying benchmark has 835 bugs across 17 projects. Full final paper explicitly says it does NOT measure paired buggy/fixed F2P fault detection and does not run mutation analysis.
SF110: 182 classes across 74 projects after token-window filtering.
Custom CMD: 31 classes across two repositories (OceanBase ODC and Conductor OSS), classes committed after May 2023 and buggy/fixed paired for contamination-resistant analysis.
task: Class-level Java JUnit test-suite generation, 30 repetitions per class and prompt/model setting, comparing GPT-3.5-Turbo, GPT-4, Mistral 7B and Mixtral 8x7B with EvoSuite across five prompts (ZSL/FSL/CoT/ToT/GToT). Evaluates raw output/extractability, syntax, compilation, readability, static smells and JaCoCo line/instruction/method coverage. Despite earlier 2024 arXiv wording and several internally inconsistent discussion sentences, the final 2026 paper's explicit Limitations section says it does not evaluate F2P bug detection, exception-oriented fault detection, or mutation-based analysis.
input_setting: Entire Java class-under-test is provided (class-level, no import injection or post-repair); generation uses five prompting strategies and a JUnit 4 output format. Defects4J classes are used for coverage/compilation/maintainability, but tests are not evaluated on paired fixed/buggy versions. Full paper says the 2026 study does not report real bug detection.
author_relationship_evidence: Final paper Data Availability section and ORBilu institutional publication page link this exact anonymous 4open repository. The repository README, however, identifies its package and citation as a 2024 anonymous study titled “Exploring Prompt Engineering…”, and repository metadata gives last update 2024-09-30/source commit date 2024-09-26. This indicates the linked artifact predates and may not exactly match the final 2026 article version.
source_commit_or_archive: Public anonymous 4open repository ID `LLM4TS-0F76`, source snapshot dated 2024-09-26 / last updated 2024-09-30; no stable git commit or source archive revision exposed. It contains MIT LICENSE, 391 bundled dependency files, Defects4J/SF110/CMD JSON datasets, raw test outputs, some RQ1/RQ2 processing results/scripts, test smell/tools and other result files. Current repository root listing contains only RQ1 and RQ2 under Experiments-Scripts-And-Results and only GPT-3.5-Turbo/EvoSuite under Generated-test-suites, despite README claiming RQ1–RQ4 plus broader model outputs. No visible RQ3/RQ4 folders or Test-Generation directory were found. README title/citation/version is 2024, not final 2026 article. Public source was inspected through 4open API (tree/list/read-only), no code executed.
license: Final article's author-accepted manuscript license statement says CC BY 4.0; Springer version-of-record is published under exclusive license. Anonymous artifact declares MIT for repository code; bundled 391 JARs and datasets/source snippets retain upstream licenses/terms.
weights_status: GPT-3.5-Turbo/GPT-4 are hosted models; Mistral 7B and Mixtral 8x7B are open weights. The paper ran temperature 0.7, 30 trials and fixed 4,096-token context for fairness. These are legacy model versions; API snapshots are not pinned. The anonymous artifact includes generated tests, not model checkpoints. User Qwen2.5-Coder is not one of the evaluated models and a full new run requires recreating the class-level harness and generation pipeline.
evaluation_route: Read the complete 58-page author manuscript (22,895 words), including all 7 research questions, results, limitations, data availability and appendices. Public 4open API confirmed MIT package/readme and visible directory inventory: datasets include Defects4J_dataset.json (~4.2 MB), SF110_dataset.json (~1.4 MB), CMD JSON; 391 dependency files; raw generated suites and partial RQ results. Author package README describes pre-generated outputs and scripts but its actual current tree lacks claimed RQ3/RQ4 and some model outputs. The exact final paper's prompt-generation/evaluation package mapping is therefore unresolved. Full original-model rerun would require legacy GPT APIs or Mistral/Mixtral hosting, 30 repeats and 477×5×models class-level suites, token filtering and old Java/dependency environments. No code/model run.
blockers: The final 2026 paper explicitly excludes paired buggy/fixed F2P detection, exception-oriented fault detection and mutation analysis. Although Defects4J is used, the primary outcome is not real bug revealability; this is weaker fit for the user's main goal.

Paper Data Availability points to an old 4open package whose README title/citation says 2024; repository source snapshot is 2024-09, before the final 2026 publication. Exact artifact-to-final-paper version mapping is unclear.

Public 4open root appears incomplete against its README/paper: only RQ1/RQ2 visible, no RQ3/RQ4 or Test-Generation directory; generated-test suite roots list only GPT-3.5-Turbo and EvoSuite. Not all final results/method scripts appear available.
No immutable versioned archive/commit for the anonymous source was found. Data and dependencies are public, but exact final pipeline/version and all generated outputs cannot be confirmed.
Original models are old/hosted in part, no exact provider snapshots; full generation is large (216,300 outputs, 30 trials) and user Qwen would be an independent model rerun.

The 2026 manuscript contains an internal inconsistency: the limitations section says no mutation/fault-detection experiments, while a later Related Work subsection says it integrates mutation testing. The actual RQ/results sections include no mutation-score or F2P results; treat the explicit limitation/results as authoritative and flag the inconsistency.
concept_fit: Moderate-high for class-level prompting and test-output reliability on Defects4J: compares five reasoning prompts, compilation/hallucination, readability and test smells, and uses whole-class generation rather than isolated methods. But it does not measure direct buggy/fixed bug detection in the final 2026 version, and it is not a concept/RCA method. Its artifact/version mismatch weakens it as a practical reproduction base.
recommendation: Read as supporting evidence about prompt effects, class-level compilation failures and maintainability; do not choose it as the primary Defects4J bug-reproduction baseline. The 2026 final paper does not provide F2P/mutation detection despite the 2024 arXiv predecessor's abstract and some discussion language. The author-linked package contains useful old data/code but is dated 2024 and visibly incomplete relative to the final article. If studying prompt engineering, use repository outputs as historical material only after mapping the exact version; for current model evaluation, prefer #74's verified reproducible Defects4J statistics or #65 for a turnkey custom-Qwen repository benchmark. No source or model run.
supporting_locations: Final paper Sections 3–4: model versions, dataset filtering, token limits, 30 repetitions, five prompting techniques and outcomes.
Final paper Section 5.2.1 Limitations and 5.2.2 Future Work: explicitly says no F2P paired-bug, exception-based fault detection, or mutation analysis; proposes these for future work.
Final paper Data Availability: links LLM4TS-0F76; author-accepted manuscript license CC BY 4.0.
Anonymous package README (saved locally at `public_evidence/author_artifact_README.md`): title/citation is 2024, claims generated tests, scripts and RQ1–RQ4.

4open repository API metadata: snapshot sourceCommitDate 2024-09-26, lastUpdateDate 2024-09-30; MIT LICENSE; 391 dependencies; Datasets/Defects4J_dataset.json; visible RQ1/RQ2 only and incomplete test suite/model directories.
Earlier arXiv/preprint 2407.00225 is a predecessor with different title and bug-detection experiments; it must not be substituted for the 2026 final article.
